hypothesis: Where a lidar-resolved step faces uphill against the regional slope and is coherent along strike, the step is more likely to be a normal-fault strand (antithetic or synthetic) than a mapped-trace artefact, so ranking cells by antislope excess places dots on unmapped fault strands better than the uniform control and better than the H33 fold-fair control.
mechanism: Antithetic normal-fault strands in extensional terrain can produce uphill-facing free faces; they are coherent along strike and expose a 10-50 m step where they offset Quaternary surfaces (Basin-and-Range normal faulting, USGS: https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-a-fault-and-what-are-different-types ; antithetic strand that forms an uphill-facing scarp, Bear River fault zone, USGS SIM 3430: https://pubs.usgs.gov/sim/3430/sim3430_pamphlet.pdf ).
named_non_fault_process: Sackung and gravitational spreading features are uphill-facing and parallel to contours and ridge crests. The literature treats them as the main confusion for tectonic uphill-facing scarps: Pyrenees sackung (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169555X0500036X), Saint Elias flexural toppling 'not tectonic faults' (https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/gsabulletin/article-abstract/122/9-10/1585/125613/Origin-of-sackung-uphill-facing-scarps-in-the?redirectedFrom=fulltext), Yakutat antislope scarps from bedding-plane normal slip (https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/geosphere/article/7/5/1143/132478/Antislope-scarps-gravitational-spreading-and). The same literature describes uphill-facing scarps as resembling the head scar of a landslide (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.3166/ga.21.187-202). The lidar product cannot separate these, so this lane's rule is expected to be weakest where sackung is common.
